title_ar: فضيلة الشيخ الددو: الأمة اليوم تجدد تاريخها وتعيد مجدها
title_en: His Eminence Sheikh al-Dedew: The Community Today Is Renewing Its History and Restoring Its Glory
body_ar:
قال فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو إن الأمة هذه الأيام تجدد تاريخها وتعيد جولة أخرى من أيامها؛ وتَصْدُق الله مرة أخرى؛ فتضحي بخيرة أبنائها، فهي أمة التضحيات، وهي خير أمة أخرت للناس.

وقال الشيخ إن ما يقع في مصر هو مرحلة من مراحل الصراع بين الحق والباطل في المعركة المستمرة إلى قيام الساعة وهذا الصراع هو إحدى سنن الله المنظمة لهذا الكون؛ لذا جعل الله الحياة مرتبطة بهذا الصراع.

وتحدث الشيخ في خطبة الجمعة اليوم 16/08/2013 بجامع مركز تكوين العلماء في عرفات بنواكشوط عن "أثر اقتحام الميادين في مصر" حيث قال إن ما يحصل في أرض الكنانة هو إعادة لمجد الأمة وتجديد لتاريخها مرة أخرى.

وأكد الشيخ خلال الخطبة أن وعد الله لهذه الأمة بالنصر هو حق لا محالة؛ مضيفا أن هذه الأمة تتلقى الضربات ولا توجعها لعلمها أن بعدها نصرا مؤزرا؛ وهو وعدٌ حق من الحق سبحانه، فقد قال الله تعالى: {ومن قتل مظلوما فقد جعلنا لوليه سلطانا فلا يسرف في القتل إنه كان منصورا}.

مبينا أن الصراع قائم أبدي، وكل يوم من أيام الدنيا هو يوم كيوم "بدر" أو "أحد" أو "حنين" أو "الأحزاب"؛ تتفاوت الأيام بحسب رجالها ولكن هدفها واحد هو التدافع بين الحق والباطل، واصفا المعتصمين في الميادين المصرية ضد الانقلاب بأنهم مرابطون في سبيل الله.

وأوضح الشيخ أنواع أهل الباطل وتعامهم مع الحق وأهله؛ حيث قال بأن أهل الباطل منهم الذين يحملون السلاح وليست لهم قلوب ولا أفئدة، ومنهم من يتكلمون بألسنة اليشاطين، لا يعجزهم كذب ولا تحريف.

وطالب فضيلة الشيخ المسلمين بالوقوف مع الحق ونصرة المظلومين والدفاع عن الدين والمقدسات، والوقوف مع قضايا الأمة العادلة، وهي فرصة - يضيف الشيخ - ليعبر فيها المؤمن عن ولائه لله ورسوله وللمؤمنين.

وبعد صلاة الجمعة أَمَّ فضيلة الشيخ الجموع التي حضرت لصلاة الغائب على شهداء مصر الذين سقطوا في مجازر اقتحام ميادين رابعة العدوية والنهضة على يد قوات الأمن المصري بمدينة القاهرة.
body_en:
His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew said that the community in these days is renewing its history and bringing round another turn of its days, and is being true to God once more, sacrificing the best of its sons; for it is the community of sacrifices, and it is the best community brought forth for mankind.

The Sheikh said that what is happening in Egypt is one stage among the stages of the struggle between truth and falsehood, in the battle that continues until the Hour arises; and that this struggle is one of God's established ways ordering this universe, which is why God has made life bound up with this struggle.

The Sheikh spoke in the Friday sermon (khuṭbah) today, 16/08/2013, at the congregational mosque of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars in Arafat in Nouakchott, on 'The Effect of the Storming of the Squares in Egypt', where he said that what is happening in the land of Kinanah is a restoration of the community's glory and a renewal of its history once again.

The Sheikh affirmed during the sermon that God's promise of victory to this community is true beyond doubt, adding that this community receives blows and they do not pain it, because it knows that after them comes a decisive victory — and it is a true promise from the True One, glorified be He; for God the Exalted has said: { And whoever is killed wrongfully, We have given his heir authority — but let him not exceed the limits in killing, for he is helped. } (Sūrat al-Isrāʾ 17:33)

He made clear that the struggle stands perpetual, and that every day of the days of this world is a day like the day of 'Badr' or of 'Uhud' or of 'Hunayn' or of 'the Confederates'; the days differ according to their men, but their purpose is one — the pushing back and forth between truth and falsehood. He described those holding the sit-ins in the Egyptian squares against the coup as men stationed in defence on God's path (murābiṭūn).

The Sheikh set out the kinds of the people of falsehood and their dealing with truth and its people, saying that among the people of falsehood are those who bear arms and who have no hearts and no inner understanding, and among them are those who speak with the tongues of devils, whom no lie and no distortion defeats.

His Eminence the Sheikh called upon the Muslims to stand with the truth, to support the wronged, to defend religion and what is held sacred, and to stand with the just causes of the community — and it is an opportunity, the Sheikh adds, in which the believer may give expression to his loyalty to God, to His Messenger and to the believers.

After the Friday prayer, His Eminence the Sheikh led the crowds who had come for the funeral prayer in absentia over the martyrs of Egypt who fell in the massacres of the storming of the Rabaa al-Adawiya and Nahda squares at the hands of the Egyptian security forces in the city of Cairo.

flags.arabic: واصفا المعتصمين في الميادين المصرية ضد الانقلاب بأنهم مرابطون في سبيل الله
flags.context: the Sheikh's characterisation of the Rabaa sit-in participants
options: men stationed in defence on God's path (murābiṭūn)
those keeping watch on the frontier for God's sake
flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW. رباط is a specific religious category — holding a frontier post against an enemy — with its own merits in the sources, and applying it to protesters facing state security forces is a substantive legal characterisation, not a figure of speech. Rendered with the Arabic visible so that the category is not lost; 'steadfast defenders' would dissolve it into English idiom. The passage, together with 'شهداء مصر' and 'الانقلاب' in the final paragraph, carries clear legal exposure in Egypt and elsewhere. Publication is for Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office to decide.

options: the best community brought forth for mankind (reading أخرت as a misprint for أُخرجت)
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT (house rule 11) in quoted scripture. The phrase alludes to { You are the best community brought forth for mankind } (Sūrat Āl ʿImrān 3:110), where the word is 'أُخرجت'. The source has 'أخرت' ('delayed'), which is not the Qur'anic word and yields a different sense. Translated by the evident sense and flagged; body_ar preserves the source. Never restore scripture from memory — this is recorded, not repaired.

flags.arabic: {ومن قتل مظلوما فقد جعلنا لوليه سلطانا فلا يسرف في القتل إنه كان منصورا}
flags.context: the verse cited in the sermon
options: an alternative rendering of سلطانا as 'a warrant' or 'a right of redress'
flags.note: Sūrat al-Isrāʾ 17:33. The verse concerns the heir's right of retaliation for wrongful killing, with a limit upon it. 'سلطان' is rendered 'authority'; 'warrant' and 'right of redress' are both defensible. Standing note: Qur'anic renderings in this corpus are interpretive and are not a substitute for the Arabic (style guide §4).

options: with the tongues of devils (reading اليشاطين as a misprint for الشياطين)
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT (house rule 11). 'اليشاطين' is not a word; 'الشياطين' (the devils) is evidently meant. Translated by the evident sense and flagged.

flags.context: وأوضح الشيخ أنواع أهل الباطل وتعامهم مع الحق وأهله
options: their dealing with truth and its people (reading تعامهم as تعاملهم)
their wilful blindness towards truth and its people (reading تعامهم from تعامى)
flags.note: Genuinely ambiguous. 'تعامُلهم' (dealing with) and 'تعامِيهم' (feigning blindness to) are both a single letter away from the printed word, and both fit the sentence. Option 0 is used because the following clause enumerates kinds of conduct rather than kinds of blindness, but the reviewer should check the sermon recording.

translator_notes: A news report of a Friday sermon delivered two days after the Rabaa dispersal; the sermon itself exists as the embedded video. Marked critical_for_display: the page compresses a sermon into slogans and a reader will take the compressed form for the Sheikh's considered position. 'أرض الكنانة' is the traditional epithet for Egypt and is rendered literally as 'the land of Kinanah'. 'صلاة الغائب' is the funeral prayer performed over an absent body. Source defects preserved in body_ar: 'أخرت' for 'أُخرجت' in quoted scripture, and 'اليشاطين' for 'الشياطين'. CMS date is a bulk-upload timestamp, not a composition date.
